# `cis_extensions.cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/cis-extensions/cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection-dry-run.satz`

## Purpose

GENERATED by scripts/build_dry_run_fragments.py from cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection.satz — do not edit.

The dry-run twin of cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection.satz. Google evaluates every rule below, writes a
violation to the audit log for each action it WOULD have blocked, and blocks
nothing — so the organisation's own numbers answer "will this break us?" before
the control is enforced. Read them in Cloud Logging:

protoPayload.metadata."@type"="type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.audit.OrgPolicyViolationInfo"

Promote by switching cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run off
and cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection on. Both on at once is refused:
the estate would declare the same policy twice, once measuring and once blocking.

This fragment carries NO claim. A dry run discharges no control while it runs, and
`require` reports the control as unmet, which is the truth.

## Use it

```
params {
  cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run = true
}

use "presets/cis-extensions/cloud-sql-iam-and-deletion-protection-dry-run.satz" when cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run
```

`cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `CIS_GCP_Foundation_4_0`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
